title: M1B Mains · Paper I · Section B · Indian Constitution (75M) › M1B.5 Centralisation vs decentralisation

syllabus_leaves.wording: Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta Committees
73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts and their Implementation

official_questions.stem: Who is regarded as the "Father of Local Self-Government" ?
official_questions.core_fact: Lord Ripon's resolution of 18 May 1882 made him the 'Father of Local Self-Government' in India.

statements.t: Lord Ripon is regarded as the 'Father of Local Self-Government'.
Lord Canning is regarded as the 'Father of Local Self-Government'.
Lord Minto is regarded as the 'Father of Local Self-Government'.
Lord Mountbatten is regarded as the 'Father of Local Self-Government'.

official_questions.rule: Ripon 1882 - local self-government; Mayo 1870 - financial decentralisation.

official_questions.stem: Who was the Prime Minister of India when Ashok Mehta Committee on Panchayati Raj was set up ?
official_questions.core_fact: The Ashok Mehta Committee was appointed in December 1977 by the Janata government of PM Morarji Desai (report Aug 1978).

statements.t: The Prime Minister when the Ashok Mehta Committee was set up was Indira Gandhi.
The Prime Minister when the Ashok Mehta Committee was set up was Morarji Desai.
The Prime Minister when the Ashok Mehta Committee was set up was Charan Singh.
The Prime Minister when the Ashok Mehta Committee was set up was V.P. Singh.

official_questions.rule: PR committees and PMs: BRM 1957 (Nehru), Ashok Mehta 1977 (Desai), GVK Rao 1985 and Singhvi 1986 (Rajiv).

official_questions.stem: In 1986, the Rajiv Gandhi Government constituted a committee on "Revitalisation of Panchayati Raj institutions for democracy and development". Who was the Chairman of the Committee ?
official_questions.core_fact: The 1986 committee on 'Revitalisation of PRIs for Democracy and Development' was chaired by L.M. Singhvi; it recommended constitutional status for PRIs.

statements.t: The Chairman of the 1986 committee on revitalisation of PRIs was Sarkaria.
The Chairman of the 1986 committee on revitalisation of PRIs was Rajamannar.
The Chairman of the 1986 committee on revitalisation of PRIs was G.V.K. Rao.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

statements.t: The Chairman of the 1986 committee on revitalisation of PRIs was L.M. Singhvi.

official_questions.rule: 1985 GVK Rao (bureaucratisation, 'grass without roots'); 1986 Singhvi (constitutional status).

official_questions.stem: One of the following was not a feature of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 :
official_questions.core_fact: The 73rd Amendment provides Gram Sabha (243A), a three-tier system (243B; intermediate tier optional below 20 lakh population), SEC (243K) and one-third reservation for women (243D).

statements.t: Gram Sabha was a feature of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act 1992.
Two-tier System was a feature of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act 1992.
State Election Commission was a feature of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act 1992.
Reservation of Seats for Women was a feature of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act 1992.

official_questions.rule: 73rd: three tiers (village, intermediate, district); small states (<20 lakh) may skip the middle tier.

official_questions.stem: Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains ______ functional items.
official_questions.core_fact: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects for panchayats (Art 243G).

statements.t: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 functional items.
The Eleventh Schedule contains 18 functional items.
statements.m: true fact not the one asked

statements.t: The Eleventh Schedule contains 26 functional items.
The Eleventh Schedule contains 28 functional items.

official_questions.rule: Eleventh = 29 (panchayats); Twelfth = 18 (municipalities).

official_questions.stem: The first Municipal Corporation in India was set up at
official_questions.core_fact: India's first municipal corporation was set up at Madras in 1688; Bombay and Calcutta followed in 1726.

statements.t: The first Municipal Corporation in India was set up at Calcutta.
The first Municipal Corporation in India was set up at Delhi.
The first Municipal Corporation in India was set up at Madras.
The first Municipal Corporation in India was set up at Jaipur.

official_questions.rule: Urban bodies: Madras 1688; Bombay and Calcutta 1726; Ripon 1882.

official_questions.stem: Twelfth Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains ______ functional items.
official_questions.core_fact: The Twelfth Schedule lists 18 functional items for municipalities (Art 243W).

statements.t: The Twelfth Schedule contains 20 functional items.
The Twelfth Schedule contains 19 functional items.
The Twelfth Schedule contains 16 functional items.
The Twelfth Schedule contains 18 functional items.

official_questions.rule: Eleventh = 29, Twelfth = 18.

official_questions.stem: Who was the Chairman of the Grow More Food Inquiry Committee ?
official_questions.core_fact: V.T. Krishnamachari chaired the Grow More Food Enquiry Committee (1952), which led to the CDP and NES.

official_questions.stem: Ashok Mehta Committee recommended the ______ tier system of Panchayati Raj.
official_questions.core_fact: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a two-tier system: Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat.

official_questions.stem: By which Constitutional Amendment Act, were Municipalities given Constitutional status (by inserting in Part IX A) ?
official_questions.core_fact: The 74th Amendment Act 1992 inserted Part IXA (Arts 243P-243ZG) giving municipalities constitutional status.

statements.t: Municipalities were given constitutional status (Part IXA) by the 73rd Amendment.
Municipalities were given constitutional status (Part IXA) by the 40th Amendment.

official_questions.stem: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee submitted its report in
official_questions.core_fact: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (appointed Jan 1957) reported in November 1957, recommending democratic decentralisation (three tiers).

official_questions.stem: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act is not applicable to which of the States given below?
options: Mizoram, Nagaland and Jammu and Kashmir

official_questions.core_fact: The 73rd Amendment (in force 24 April 1993) inserted Part IX: Articles 243 to 243-O (16 articles) and the Eleventh Schedule.

The 73rd Amendment added 9 articles.
The 73rd Amendment added 12 articles.
The 73rd Amendment added 16 articles.

official_questions.stem: As per Article 243 of the Constitution, the following would be the members of "Gram Sabha"
options: All adults with age of 18 years and above in the Panchayat area
All voters as per electoral rolls relating to the Panchayat area
All citizens residing in the Panchayat
All persons allowed by the Gram Panchayat

statements.t: As per Article 243, members of the Gram Sabha are All adults with age of 18 years and above in the Panchayat area.
statements.d: All adults with age of 18 years and above in the Panchayat area
statements.fact: Gram Sabha = all persons on the electoral rolls of the Panchayat area.

statements.t: As per Article 243, members of the Gram Sabha are All voters as per electoral rolls relating to the Panchayat area.

statements.t: As per Article 243, members of the Gram Sabha are All citizens residing in the Panchayat.

official_questions.stem: The Martandam rural reconstruction programme was based on certain principles known as..............
official_questions.core_fact: The Martandam rural reconstruction project (1921, Spencer Hatch, YMCA, Travancore) aimed at fivefold (spirit, mind, body, social, economic) development; APPSC deleted the question.

statements.t: The Martandam rural reconstruction programme was based on certain principles known as [no key - deleted].

official_questions.rule: Pre-1952 experiments: Sriniketan (Tagore 1921), Martandam (Hatch 1921), Gurgaon (Brayne 1927), Etawah (Mayer 1948), Nilokheri (Dey).
official_questions.key_note: Deleted by APPSC; no key; statement U.

official_questions.stem: "The extension worker translates the scientific findings of the laboratories in such a way that the farm families can voluntarily adopt them to satisfy their needs." This is called
official_questions.key: Principle of applied science and democratic approach
official_questions.core_fact: An extension principle: the worker translates laboratory findings into practice (applied science) so farm families adopt them voluntarily (democratic approach).

statements.t: Translating research so farmers voluntarily adopt it is the principle of applied science and democratic approach.

official_questions.rule: Extension principles include interest/need, cultural difference, participation, applied science, democratic approach, learning by doing.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following methods provides best opportunity to re-examine one's own as well as others point of view, feelings, behavior and experiences?
official_questions.core_fact: Role play is an experiential training method in which participants act out others' roles, enabling them to re-examine their own and others' viewpoints, feelings, behaviour and experiences.

statements.t: Role play provides the best opportunity to re-examine one's own as well as others' point of view, feelings, behaviour and experiences.

official_questions.rule: Methods: lecture (knowledge), demonstration (skill), role play (attitudes/empathy), case study (analysis).

official_questions.stem: Which Committee first suggested Constitutional Status for Panchayati Raj Institutions:
official_questions.core_fact: The L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) recommended that Panchayati Raj institutions be constitutionally recognised, protected and preserved; earlier, Ashok Mehta (1978) suggested constitutional recognition only in general terms.

statements.t: The L.M. Singhvi Committee first suggested constitutional status for Panchayati Raj Institutions.

official_questions.rule: PRI committees: Balwant Rai Mehta 1957 (3-tier), Ashok Mehta 1978 (2-tier), GVK Rao 1985, L.M. Singhvi 1986 (constitutional status), Thungon 1988.
official_questions.key_note: Key kept. Many texts credit the Ashok Mehta Committee (1978) with first suggesting constitutional recognition; L.M. Singhvi (1986) made the explicit constitutional-status recommendation.

official_questions.stem: How many Municipalities are there in Andhra Pradesh at present:
official_questions.core_fact: Per APPSC's 2019 key, Andhra Pradesh had 71 municipalities (excluding municipal corporations and nagar panchayats) at the time; the count has changed with later upgradations.

statements.t: In 2019 Andhra Pradesh had 71 municipalities.

official_questions.rule: AP ULB counts change with upgradation - always date the figure.

official_questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of Direct Democracy?
official_questions.core_fact: In the Gram Sabha all voters of the village participate directly in deliberation (approving plans, identifying beneficiaries), making it an instance of direct democracy within a representative system.

statements.t: The Grama Sabha is an example of direct democracy.

official_questions.rule: Direct democracy in India: Gram Sabha; instruments elsewhere: referendum, initiative, recall, plebiscite.

official_questions.stem: Which of the Article provide for the Reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Panchayat Raj Institutions:
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 243D: reservation of seats for SCs and STs in proportion to population in every Panchayat, not less than one-third for women, and of chairpersons' offices.

statements.t: Article 243D provides for reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Panchayat Raj institutions.

official_questions.rule: Part IX: 243A Gram Sabha, 243B three tiers, 243C composition, 243D reservation, 243E 5-year term, 243K SEC.

official_questions.stem:
Match list-I (Functionaries) with list-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below lists:
List-I (Functionaries) / List-II (Institution)
A. Sarpanch - 1. Municipal Corporation
B. Chairperson - 2. Village Panchayat
C. Mayor - 3. Municipality
D. Councillor - 4. Cantonment Board
5. Ward
official_questions.core_fact: A Sarpanch heads a village panchayat, a Chairperson a municipality, a Mayor a municipal corporation; a Councillor represents a ward.

statements.t: The Sarpanch is the functionary of the Village Panchayat.
The Chairperson is the functionary of the Municipality.
The Mayor is the functionary of the Municipal Corporation.
The Councillor is the representative of a Ward.

official_questions.rule: Rural: Sarpanch/MPP President/ZP Chairperson; Urban: Chairperson (municipality), Mayor (corporation), Councillor (ward).

official_questions.stem: Gram Panchayat meetings are convened by
official_questions.core_fact: Per APPSC's key, Gram Panchayat meetings are convened by the Panchayat Secretary (who issues notices on the Sarpanch's direction) under the AP Panchayat Raj Act 1994 and rules.

statements.t: Gram Panchayat meetings are convened by the Panchayat Secretary.

official_questions.rule: AP GP: Sarpanch presides, Secretary convenes/executes; Gram Sabha meets at least twice a year (AP).

official_questions.stem: A Gram Sabha at the village level is:
official_questions.key: An assembly where all registered voters of the village are members
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 243(b): Gram Sabha means a body of persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the area of a Panchayat; Art. 243A: it exercises powers the State legislature gives.

statements.t: A Gram Sabha at the village level is an assembly in which all registered voters of the village are members.

official_questions.rule: Gram Sabha = all voters of the village (Art. 243(b)); the only direct-democracy organ of PRIs.

official_questions.stem: Community Development Programme was initiated to:
official_questions.key: Contribute to development of village through public participation
official_questions.core_fact: The CDP (2 Oct 1952) sought all-round village development through people's participation; its failure led to the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957).

statements.t: The Community Development Programme was initiated to contribute to the development of villages through public participation.

official_questions.rule: CDP 1952 + NES 1953 -> BRM Committee 1957 -> PRI 1959 (Nagaur).

official_questions.stem: The Governor of Andhra Pradesh has appointed ______ of the gram panchayat as the Marriage officer.
official_questions.core_fact: Under the AP Compulsory Registration of Marriages Act 2002 and its notification, the Panchayat Secretary of the gram panchayat is the marriage registering officer for the village (per APPSC key).

statements.t: The Governor of Andhra Pradesh has appointed the Panchayat Secretary of the gram panchayat as the Marriage Officer.

official_questions.rule: AP village level: Panchayat Secretary = registrar of births/deaths and marriages.

official_questions.stem:
Assertion (A) : The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act is a significant landmark in the evolution of grassroots democratic institutions in the country.
Reason (R) : This Act has brought the Panchayath Raj institutions under the purview of justiciable part of the Constitution.
options: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
official_questions.key: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
official_questions.core_fact: The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave PRIs constitutional status in Part IX, shifting them from the non-justiciable DPSP (Art. 40) to justiciable provisions binding the States - hence a landmark in grassroots democracy.

statements.t: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act is a significant landmark in the evolution of grassroots democratic institutions in the country.
The Act brought Panchayati Raj institutions under the purview of the justiciable part of the Constitution.
R explains A: being brought under the justiciable part is why the 73rd Amendment is a landmark.

official_questions.rule: 73rd Amd: Art. 40 (DPSP) converted into binding Part IX; States must hold elections every 5 years.

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statements is/are not correct regarding the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act ?
A. 18 functional items were placed within the purview of Panchayats.
B. The Act does not apply to the States of Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram.
C. The Act bars interference by courts in the electoral matters of Panchayats.
D. Reservation of seats to BCs is a compulsory provision under this Act.
official_questions.core_fact: 73rd Amendment: Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects (Twelfth Schedule for municipalities: 18); Part IX does not apply to Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram and certain areas (Art. 243M); courts barred in electoral matters (Art. 243O); BC reservation is voluntary (Art. 243D(6)).

statements.t: Under the 73rd Amendment 18 functional items were placed within the purview of Panchayats.
statements.fact: The Eleventh Schedule has 29 items; 18 is the Twelfth Schedule (municipalities).

statements.t: The 73rd Amendment does not apply to the States of Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram.
The 73rd Amendment bars interference by courts in the electoral matters of Panchayats.
Reservation of seats for BCs is a compulsory provision under the 73rd Amendment.
statements.fact: Reservation for backward classes is a voluntary provision left to State legislatures (Art. 243D(6)).

official_questions.rule: Compulsory: Gram Sabha, 3 tiers, direct election, SC/ST + 1/3 women, 5-yr term, SEC, SFC; Voluntary: BC reservation, MP/MLA representation, devolution of 29 items.

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following statements about State Finance Commission is/are correct ?
i. This Commission examines the financial position of the local governments in the State.
ii. It also reviews the distribution of revenues between the State and Local governments on the one hand and between rural and urban local governments on the other.
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 243-I/243Y: the Governor constitutes an SFC every 5 years to review the financial position of panchayats and municipalities and recommend distribution of State taxes between the State and local bodies, and among levels, and grants-in-aid.

statements.t: The State Finance Commission examines the financial position of the local governments in the State.
The State Finance Commission reviews the distribution of revenues between the State and local governments and between rural and urban local governments.

official_questions.rule: SFC: Governor constitutes every 5 years (243-I); Union FC recommends augmenting State funds for local bodies (280(3)(bb),(c)).

official_questions.stem: Regarding the Panchayat Raj System, in 1978 Ashok Mehta Committee recommended for
options: two tier system with four years of term
three tier system with four years of term
two tier system with five years of term
three tier system with six years of term
official_questions.key: two tier system with four years of term
official_questions.core_fact: The Ashok Mehta Committee (Janata govt, 1977-78) recommended a two-tier system (Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat) with a four-year term, open party participation and constitutional recognition.

statements.t: In 1978 the Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a two tier system with four years of term.
statements.d: two tier system with four years of term

statements.t: In 1978 the Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a three tier system with four years of term.
statements.d: three tier system with four years of term
statements.fact: Ashok Mehta recommended two tiers (Balwant Rai Mehta had three).

statements.t: In 1978 the Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a two tier system with five years of term.
statements.d: two tier system with five years of term
statements.fact: Ashok Mehta's term was four years; five years came with the 73rd Amendment.

statements.t: In 1978 the Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a three tier system with six years of term.
statements.d: three tier system with six years of term
statements.fact: Ashok Mehta: two tiers, four years.

official_questions.rule: BRM 1957: 3 tiers; Ashok Mehta 1978: 2 tiers, 4 yrs; 73rd Amd: 3 tiers (2 for <20 lakh), 5 yrs.

official_questions.stem:
Which of the following provisions of 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act related to Panchayat Raj Institutions is/are correct ?
i. The members of these bodies are directly elected by the people.
ii. Elections shall be held within a period of 3 months from the dissolution of the body.
iii. Women have been given 1/3rd reservation in Panchayats.
iv. The minimum age required to become member is 21 years.
official_questions.core_fact: Art. 243C(2): all seats filled by direct election; Art. 243E(3): election before expiry or within six months of dissolution; Art. 243D(3): not less than one-third seats for women; Art. 243F(1)(a): minimum age 21.

statements.t: The members of Panchayati Raj bodies are directly elected by the people.
Elections shall be held within a period of three months from the dissolution of the body.
statements.fact: Fresh elections must be completed within six months of dissolution.

statements.t: Women have been given one-third reservation in Panchayats.
The minimum age required to become a member of a Panchayat is 21 years.

official_questions.rule: 73rd Amd numbers: 5-yr term, 6 months re-election, 1/3 women, 21 years, 29 subjects, 20 lakh population for 2 tiers.

official_questions.stem: Panchayats have responsibilities in respect of which of the following as per the Eleventh Schedule ?
official_questions.core_fact: The Eleventh Schedule (Art 243G) lists 29 panchayat subjects, including libraries (item 20); slaughter houses, land-use regulation and burial grounds are Twelfth Schedule (municipal) items.

statements.t: As per the Eleventh Schedule, Panchayats have responsibility for Libraries.
As per the Eleventh Schedule, Panchayats have responsibility for Regulation of slaughter houses.
statements.fact: Slaughter houses and tanneries are a Twelfth Schedule (municipal) item.

statements.t: As per the Eleventh Schedule, Panchayats have responsibility for Regulation of land use.
statements.fact: Regulation of land use is a Twelfth Schedule item; the Eleventh has land improvement/land reforms.

statements.t: As per the Eleventh Schedule, Panchayats have responsibility for Burials and burial grounds.
statements.fact: Burials and burial grounds are a Twelfth Schedule item.

official_questions.rule: Eleventh vs Twelfth: 'regulation' items (land use, slaughter houses) and burial grounds are urban; land improvement, libraries, cultural activities are panchayat items.

official_questions.stem: Municipalities have Constitutional responsibilities in respect of which of the following as per the Twelfth Schedule ?
official_questions.core_fact: The Twelfth Schedule (Art 243W) lists 18 municipal subjects incl. cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals; non-conventional energy, small-scale industries and technical/vocational education are Eleventh Schedule items.

statements.t: As per the Twelfth Schedule, Municipalities have responsibility for Non-conventional Energy Sources.
statements.fact: Non-conventional energy sources are an Eleventh Schedule (panchayat) item.

statements.t: As per the Twelfth Schedule, Municipalities have responsibility for Cattle Pounds.
As per the Twelfth Schedule, Municipalities have responsibility for Small scale industries.
statements.fact: Small-scale industries are an Eleventh Schedule item.

statements.t: As per the Twelfth Schedule, Municipalities have responsibility for Technical Training and Vocational Education.
statements.fact: Technical training and vocational education are an Eleventh Schedule item.

official_questions.rule: Twelfth Schedule 'odd' items: cattle pounds, burials, slaughter houses, urban forestry, fire services; the rural-development items belong to the Eleventh.

official_questions.stem: The State Election Commission conducts elections to
official_questions.core_fact: Arts 243K and 243ZA: the SEC superintends, directs and controls elections to panchayats and municipalities; State Legislature elections are by the ECI (Art. 324); co-operative elections by a body under Art. 243ZK (in AP the Co-operative Election Authority).

statements.t: The State Election Commission conducts elections to Local Bodies.
The State Election Commission conducts elections to State Legislatures.
statements.fact: State Legislature elections are conducted by the ECI (Art. 324).

statements.t: The State Election Commission conducts elections to Primary Agricultural Co-operative Societies.
statements.fact: Co-operative society elections are by the authority under Art. 243ZK / State Co-operative Acts.

statements.t: The State Election Commission conducts elections to Co-operative Banks.
statements.fact: Co-operative bank elections are not conducted by the SEC.

official_questions.rule: ECI: Parliament, legislatures, President, VP; SEC: panchayats + municipalities.

official_questions.stem:
Arrange the following Committees of Panchayat Raj in chronological order.
a. Gadgil Committee
b. Dantwala Committee
c. L. M. Singhvi Committee
d. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
official_questions.core_fact: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957) -> Dantwala (1978, block-level planning) -> L.M. Singhvi (1986) -> Gadgil (1988, Sarkaria-era policy committee recommending constitutional status).

statements.t: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) preceded the Dantwala Committee (1978).
The Dantwala Committee (1978) preceded the L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986).
The L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) preceded the Gadgil Committee (1988).

official_questions.rule: PRI committees: BRM 1957, Ashok Mehta 1977-78, Dantwala 1978, Hanumantha Rao 1984, GVK Rao 1985, Singhvi 1986, Thungon 1988, Gadgil 1988.

official_questions.stem: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 came into force on
official_questions.core_fact: The 74th Amendment (Nagarpalikas) came into force on 1 June 1993; the 73rd came into force on 24 April 1993 (National Panchayati Raj Day).

statements.m: true fact not the one asked
statements.fact: 24 April 1993 is the 73rd Amendment's commencement; the 74th came into force on 1 June 1993.

statements.fact: The 74th came into force on 1 June 1993.

statements.t: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 came into force on 1st June, 1993.
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 came into force on 24th April, 1992.
statements.fact: The 74th came into force on 1 June 1993.

official_questions.rule: 73rd: 24 Apr 1993 (Panchayati Raj Day); 74th: 1 June 1993.
